top_choice_rationale: P003 rests on the most mature, independently reproduced and quantitatively benchmarked body of work among the proposals: the Jaksch-Zoller proposal, the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy realised engineered Hubbard-type many-body Hamiltonians, with no dependence on an unsettled mechanism. The citation can be kept distinct from 2001 and 2012 by centring it on strongly correlated lattice matter and imaging. The credit (Zoller for theory, Bloch and Greiner for experiments) is the weakest point, since Cirac, Jaksch, Esslinger and Bakr have arguable claims, but I judge the physics clearer than the open pairing mechanism and attribution edges of P001 and the null-test and lineage question of P002. P001 is second, P002 third; any award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile for the laureates in P001-P003; I work in nearby areas of quantum technology (circuit and waveguide QED, quantum simulation and computing) and direct WACQT, but the profile records no collaboration with the proposed laureates.
